title: Correct f2 magnitude
description: Essential: Student must state that the friction force from ground on B equals the applied force F1 = 14 N because the system is at rest and F1 is less than maximum static friction.

title: Correct f1 magnitude
description: Essential: Student must state that the friction force B exerts on A is 0 N, as A experiences no net horizontal force when at rest relative to B.

title: Correct F2 magnitude
description: Essential: Student must calculate F2 = 2μmg = 16 N for constant velocity motion, equaling the total kinetic friction on both blocks.

title: Correct elastic force
description: Essential: Student must calculate the elastic (contact) force A exerts on B as μmg = 8 N, balancing the friction on B.

title: Apply Newton's First Law
description: Important: Student correctly applies Newton's First Law (zero net force) to analyze equilibrium or constant velocity for each block.

title: Use friction formulas
description: Important: Student correctly uses kinetic friction formula f = μN and identifies when static friction equals applied force.

title: Free-body diagram reasoning
description: Optional: Student uses free-body diagrams or explicitly identifies forces on each block to set up equations.

title: Unit consistency
description: Optional: Student includes correct units (N) with numerical answers or shows unit analysis in steps.

title: Confuse static/kinetic friction
description: Pitfall: Student incorrectly uses kinetic friction for part (1) when blocks are stationary, or misapplies maximum static friction.

title: Sign or direction error
description: Pitfall: Student makes a sign error in force equations, or incorrectly assumes internal friction between A and B in part (1).
